column3: Close to the Hebrew.
NASB supplies “anything like”; “ancestors” is rendered “fathers.”
“Children” is rendered “sons.”
The Hebrew uses four different locust words; NASB distinguishes them as “gnawing,” “swarming,” “creeping,” and “stripping” locust.
Close to the Hebrew.
“Has come up on” is rendered “has invaded.”
“Vines” and “fig trees” are rendered in the singular; “stump” is rendered “splinters.”
“Husband” is rendered “bridegroom.”
“Drink offering” is rendered “libation,” and “servants” “ministers.”
“Devastated” is rendered “ruined”; the Hebrew “ground dried up” (or “mourns”) is rendered “The land mourns,” and “dried out” “fails.”
“Perished” is rendered “destroyed.”
“Dried out” is rendered “fails,” and “children of humankind” “sons of men”; NASB adds “Indeed.”
NASB supplies “with sackcloth” after “Gird yourselves”; “servants” is rendered “ministers,” and “drink offering” “libation.”
“Call an assembly” is rendered “Proclaim a solemn assembly”; NASB adds “To.”
“Devastation” is rendered “destruction.”
“Joy and rejoicing” is rendered “Gladness and joy.”
“Shovels” is rendered “clods”; the Hebrew words are rare and the meaning is uncertain. “Granaries” is rendered “barns.”
“Livestock” is rendered “beasts,” and “wandered in confusion” “wander aimlessly.”
“Call” is rendered “cry,” and “set ablaze” “burned up.”
“Channels of water” is rendered “water brooks.”
